sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and sample values
sections.what: Imports the settings reader and declares a sample database address and a long sample secret.
sections.why: Gives the tests realistic but fake values to check against.
sections.watch_out: The sample values are for tests only and must never be used in a real environment.

sections.name: env
sections.title: Settings checks
sections.what: Checks that the database address is required and must be a PostgreSQL address. Checks that the secret must be at least 32 characters in production only. Checks that the site address is a full URL or unset, with empty values treated as unset. Checks the feature defaults: live calls off, prototype data on outside production, language model off without a key, seeding off. Checks production turns prototype data off unless it is set explicitly, that admin emails are split and cleaned, that seeding is refused in production, and that all problems are reported in one error.
sections.why: Likely reason: a wrong setting in production could expose test data or leave the app open, so the checks catch these early.
sections.watch_out: The defaults decide what visitors see. A change to a default flag can silently turn on prototype or live features.

summary: Tests the environment settings reader, which checks the app's configuration values when it starts and decides which features are on by default.
purpose: Makes sure the app refuses to start with missing or unsafe settings and that the safe defaults are used when settings are absent.
why: Likely reason: settings such as the secret and the data flags control security and what visitors see, so mistakes must stop startup.
how: Passes sets of settings into the reader and checks it accepts good values, rejects bad ones with clear messages, reports all problems together, and applies the defaults and production rules.
inputs: Sample settings such as the database address, the secret, the site address, the admin list and the feature flags.
outputs: A checked settings object, or an error that names the setting that is wrong.
risks: Defaults decide what is live or shown. Changing a default, such as prototype data being on, can expose data that should be hidden.
debug: Read the error message, which names the setting. Compare the sample values with the production rules in the test.
